title: Evaluation of head-mounted displays for intraoperative visualization of CT, MRI, and endoscopy images
summary:
During surgeries, important visual information—such as CT scans or images from camera systems—has traditionally been displayed on separate monitors. As a result, surgeons must regularly look away from the surgical site to view this information. This can disrupt their concentration and lead to poor posture and fatigue.

So-called head-mounted displays (HMDs) are portable screens worn directly in front of the eyes. They allow medical imaging information to be displayed directly in the surgeon’s field of view, reducing the need to shift their gaze. This could improve working conditions in the operating room.

The aim of this study is to investigate how well such systems can be used in everyday clinical practice. Aspects such as usability, comfort, potential discomfort (e.g., eye strain or dizziness), and technical reliability will be evaluated. The study takes place during actual surgeries, as important factors such as time pressure, team communication, and workflows can only be realistically assessed in that setting. The results are intended to help better evaluate the benefits and practical applicability of head-mounted displays in surgery.
conditions: No clinical presentation; visualization of imaging data via HMDs

interventions.name: The surgeon conducts the study using an HMD and completes questionnaires at the end, as described under primary endpoints. Patients undergo surgery in accordance with the guidelines or their specific condition. The difference is that the surgeon views the imaging necessary for the surgery via the HM

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
▪    Clinical staff with surgical experience who are actively involved in performing the procedures.
▪    Written consent to participate in the study and to use a head-mounted display (HMD).
▪    Sufficient knowledge of German to understand the informed consent process and sufficient knowledge of English to complete standardized questionnaires (such as SUS, ISONORM 9241-110-S).
▪    Prior brief trial use of the HMD outside the operating room without any relevant complaints (e.g., severe nausea, dizziness, disorientation, headaches).
Exclusion criteria:
▪    No consent or withdrawal of consent to participate in the study or use the HMD.
▪    Insufficient language skills (German/English) to understand the informed consent form and complete the questionnaires.
▪    Occurrence of relevant symptoms (e.g., motion sickness, pronounced visual fatigue, disorientation, headaches) during the preceding test use; in this case, the combination of this surgeon and the respective HMD model will not be used in the operating room.
▪    Should subjective symptoms or impairments arise during the procedure that, in the surgeon’s assessment, could compromise the safe performance of the surgery, the use of the HMD by that individual will be terminated immediately; the headset will be removed, and the procedure will continue without the HMD according to routine protocol.
